notes: Local corrections of the generated land where the frozen 2023 USGS raster predates what was built (tools/lib/terrain-overrides.mjs). World metres: +X east, +Z south.

A site's scope is its OSM areas plus traced polygons (add_xz), minus corridors round protected ways (exclude_ways: half_width_m each side; a single-way entry may list spans, metres along the way from its first node, where the left or right side of its direction is narrower; along a span the land leaves that join kept and corrected ground are 1 m, so the way's own ground more than 1.5 m inside the narrowed edge stays exactly as generated) and traced polygons (exclude_xz), inside the land. The correction fades to exactly zero over edge_blend_m at the scope's edge, so the land outside the scope and on the coastline keeps its generated surface.

The site's grade is a harmonic membrane on a grid_m grid (relaxation over-relaxation factor, a fixed number of iterations): it takes the generated land outside the scope and the level and profile targets inside their shapes, and is as smooth as possible everywhere else, so the 32 m land grid's waves smooth out and designed surfaces meet their surroundings in gentle ramps. Regions apply in order: level holds a flat elevation_m inside its shape, profile holds control elevations_m along its line, sink cuts depth_m below the grade with a smoothstep rim side_run_m wide. Shapes: points_xz (optionally grown by buffer_m, negative to inset), line_xz with width_m, or an ellipse (center_xz, radii_m, rotation_deg turning +X toward +Z).

Every 32 m land cell the correction reaches is re-meshed as a quadtree of leaves down to min_leaf_m, split until each leaf's two triangles stay within tolerance_m of the corrected surface (sampled every sample_m); shared edges stay watertight, coarse neighbours keep their surface.
All elevations, depths and rims here are production inference for game art, traced from the designer's plan and dated photos, not survey data.

sites.name: Cityside Park

The 2023 USGS raster (CA_SanFrancisco_B23) predates the 2024-2025 grading: it shows a pit where the lawn is and fill mounds along the future promenade. The lot south-east of the park, fenced until 2026, is built as a park (owner video 2026-11-15): its wedge by the notch, its north-west corner and its north part join the scope (all but a strip along Isle House's land cell, whose shared edge the re-meshed cells fan to), its north tip and north-west end are levelled where the 2023 raster still has the fill stockpile, and its mound is a raise.

The park's north tip and north-west end are flat where the 2023 USGS raster still has the fill stockpile (up to about 8 m): level at about the lawn's height (owner video 2026-11-15, f_000-f_005 the flat north tip; f_051, f_090, f_103, f_107, f_112 a low lawn mound with cars seen over its crest). Height production inference. Between this level and the avenue's west sidewalk the grade falls from just behind the sidewalk (the avenue corridor's span): the sidewalk and the carriageway stand on the raster's hump, up to 2.0 m above this level, and keep their generated ground.

The park outside Isle House's raised lawn at its north-west end, its mulch slope with the chairs falling to the bike path (owner video 2026-11-15, f_100-f_110). Height about 1 m and extent are production inference: the frames show the slope from the bike path, not the mound's top or north-east side.

Cityside's cycle-track leg beside the park outside Isle House (w1530615890, from just north of its bend by the pump station to its south end at the bike path: the concrete ribbon on the way, the mulch strip, Cityside's asphalt track and the bioretention bed's rim beside it) stays at the heights main's generated land gives it (a23ed049, 2026-11-16): the line visits every node of this site's 1 m grade grid in that strip, one vertex per node with main's land height there (on the rim with the bed's cut added back, as a sink cuts from the grade), so the grade holds main's surface node for node, and the rest of the bed, the swale and the forebay west of it relax back to main's grade. Without it the park's levelled north end (isle_house_park_north_grade) pulled the corner down by up to 0.9 m. Heights are main's generated land, not survey data.

Where the park's levelled north end (4.7 m) meets the held cycle-track strip (cityside_track_leg_hold, up to about 6.1 m at its east edge, on the 2023 stockpile's flank as main has it), the ground east of the strip stays at the strip's edge height for 1 m and then falls at 1 in 4 (14 degrees) to the level instead of a step, one vertex per node of the 1 m grade grid, with leaves down to 1 m so the mesh follows the bank's top: a bank up to about 1.4 m high and 6.7 m wide beside the track along about 16 to 52 m of the leg from its bend. The owner's video shows this ground level with the track (f_107, f_112); the bank is the cost of keeping Cityside's corner at main's heights. Production inference.
